I worked for a major ISP doing tech support for two years and have lots of war stories. Ask me about funny customers or troubleshooting process or just how to deal with people in call centers.

I am former tech support for a major ISP/Cable company. Ever wonder what really happens when you call in about slow internet, sports blackouts, sudden loss of phone service? Ask me anything.
What really happens when I call in about slow internet, sports blackouts, and sudden loss of phone service?

My favorite. Alright, first thing happens is you go through the call queue. The automated system will walk you through some basics to expedite the amount of time you're on the phone with a human and possibly resolve your issue. After that a techs phone will ring with you on the other end.

Here comes our first variable. If you got a good tech they will pick up the phone and ask your phone number. If you got a bad tech they will pick up and instantly hang up to increase their call volume with no real effort.

Next variable, if you got a good tech they will ask you about your issue. They will ask you what troubleshooting you've already performed and ask you how long you've been experiencing this. They will ensure you are not on a wireless connection. If you are on a wireless connection they will tell you to get on a wired connection or screw off. Then they will ask you to run a speedtest. Then based on the results they will typically ask you to run a javascript application in your browser. This will typically resolve the issue. In worse cases they may have to involve a network engineer or a field tech.

Alternatively if you get a bad tech they will do random troubleshooting hoping you can't tell how ignorant they are until the call gets escalated to the next level tech. Hopefully the next level tech will resolve your issue. It is rare that a field tech is needed for slow throughput and even more rare that one can even fix it so if they rush to that answer they probably don't know what they're doing.
